author: Tampa Bay Times
title: Cole Sulser lands on IL with back issue, Chris Roycroft rejoins Rays - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago Rays reliever Cole Sulser heads to the injured list with lower back spasms, but isn't expected to be out long. [ LUIS SANTANA | Times ] Chris Roycroft spent his Wednesday morning in Durham, North Carolina. By 4 p.m., he was back at the Trop fine-tuning pitch grips.
The Rays had optioned Roycroft to Triple-A Durham on Saturday, hours after he picked up his first career save in Friday’s 11-3 win over Cleveland. The right-hander flew back to Tampa at 10 a.m. on Wednesday morning.
“I made it all the way down and then turned back around,” he said, clearly appreciative of the change of plans.
Roycroft was acquired from St. Louis in a June 23 trade and called up by the Rays on July 6. He made six appearances, with a 5.54 ERA and the one save.
He returned to replace Cole Sulser, who was put on the 15-day injured list with lower back spasms. Sulser, one of the Rays’ most used relievers, has a 4.86 ERA over 41 games, with a 1-0 record and two saves.
Sulser had a separate 12-day stint on the injured list for similar back issues in late May. Manager Kevin Cash said that, like last time, Sulser should return quickly.
Shane McClanahan ready to start Shane McClanahan is coming off a solid Friday start against the Guardians. [ HANNAH WALLS | Times ] After recovering from a rough start against the Red Sox and throwing well against the Guardians, Shane McClanahan said he’s excited to pitch against the Rangers on Thursday.
“I feel like I learn more from my failures, and that Boston outing really showed me that I gotta get ahead, gotta compete and get back in that rhythm,” he said. “It just shows how important that consistency is, and I’ve been in a really good routine.”
McClanahan said he focused on giving himself grace for the earlier pitching hiccup. Settling back into his weekly habits paid off against Cleveland, and he hopes it will do the same against a fierce Rangers squad.
“Going into last week, I put a really good week together, and I feel like I’m putting a good week together right now,” McClanahan said. “I’m ready to get out there and compete.”
Another Bryan Baker save Rays reliever Bryan Baker high-fives first baseman Jonathan Aranda after the final out Wednesday night. [ LUIS SANTANA | Times ] Closer Bryan Baker converted his 18th consecutive save opportunity, the third-longest active streak in the majors and the eighth-longest streak in franchise history. His 29 saves are the second most in the league, behind Cleveland’s Cade Smith.
“He’s been so impressive, and he’s not a guy that’s got a lot of saves coming into the season,” Cash said. “Some spotty opportunities here or there, but he has really settled into that role pitching the back end of our game.”
Baker’s teammates echoed the sentiment.
“I don’t want to face him. He’s gross,” Rays outfielder Ryan Vilade said. “I’m glad he’s on our team, and whenever we get to the ninth with him on the bump, we feel pretty good.”
It’s a small world You could say the Rays' Ryan Vilade has some history with the Rangers organization. [ HANNAH WALLS | Times ] Having Texas in town is nostalgic for Vilade, who has family history with the Rangers.
Vilade’s father spent six seasons coaching with the Rangers’ Double-A affiliate, and Vilade grew up learning from players such as Elvis Andrus, Rougned Odor and Joey Gallo. He also worked as a bat boy when Rays starter Nick Martinez was on the Frisco (Texas) team — something both players remembered fondly when they met again on the Cincinnati Reds last season.
“It was awesome,” said Martinez, noting that he’s since appreciated getting to see Vilade come out of his shell since being called up to the majors. “He was real quiet in Cincinnati. He’s definitely opened up a little bit more.”
“It’s funny how the baseball world works,” Vilade said. “Glad we can be on each others’ team and share each and every day together.”
Rosy history aside, Vilade clarified that he would be all business on the field against the Rangers.
“It helped me learn the game, being there when I was a kid,” Vilade said. “Now, we’re trying to beat them.”
Miscellany Reliever Manny Rodríguez pitched in Durham on Wednesday afternoon, throwing one scoreless inning with one hit and one strikeout. It was his first Triple-A appearance since elbow surgery last August. ... Wednesday’s game was the first in Rays history in which every hit from both teams was an extra-base hit (seventh time overall in modern era). The tally? Seven hits total (five doubles, two homers).
